feature: The paint bucket fills the enclosed area you click
summary: Clicking with the Fill tool inside lines on a picture now fills just the area the lines enclose, the way Photoshop's paint bucket does. Before, it turned the whole picture one colour and the lines disappeared.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/bucket-fills-the-enclosed-area-walk.json.

try.do: Before this change, with your steps: four lines merged down, the Fill tool clicked inside. The whole picture went the fill colour and the lines were gone.
Draw four lines that cross at the corners with the Line tool, pressing Command E after each to merge it into the Background.
Press G for the Fill tool and click inside the box. Only the box fills, right up to the lines.
Press Command Z once. The whole fill goes back.
Draw a box whose bottom line stops short and click inside it. The fill leaks out through the gap, as Photoshop's would.
Untick Contiguous in the bar above the tools and click again. Every pixel of that colour on the layer fills, joined or not.
Draw a rectangle and click it with the bucket. It still takes the colour whole, as before.

evaluate: Does the fill meet the lines cleanly, with no pale ring between line and fill?
Is Tolerance 32 the right default for screenshots, or do you find yourself raising it?
Are Tolerance, Anti-alias and Contiguous where you look for them, in the bar above the tools and the Fill Tool section of the panel?
Should the bucket also offer Photoshop's All Layers, so it can fill using lines that sit on another layer?
rough: Your report said the fill 'ends up not filling the whole screen'. In the reproduction, the old bucket filled the WHOLE picture and wiped the lines (first picture), so I read the report as the bucket not filling just the shape. If you saw something else, say so on this line.

Measured on the walk's picture (lines about 3 px wide): 306,767 pixels flooded, 0 white pixels left inside, 0 left along the lines, 0 pixels changed outside the box. The unit tests measure the same for a 1 px anti-aliased line.
The bucket reads only the layer you click, like Photoshop's default. Lines on a layer of their own, above an unmerged picture, do not stop it. There is no All Layers switch yet.
A picture that has been cropped or turned still takes the colour whole, as before. Only a plain picture floods.
With a marquee up, the bucket still fills the whole marquee rather than flooding inside it.
No mock covers the bucket's settings. They follow the Tool options row of the placement table (UX-PATTERNS, placement contract), beside the wand's Tolerance.
